research.headline: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
research.summary: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) achieve remarkable success on diverse multimodal understanding and generation tasks, yet they still struggle to effectively leverage language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation. As a result, existing reasoning-augmented UMMs often fail to inherit the test-time scaling and fine-grained controllability observed in large language models. We attribute this failure to a fundamental modality mismatch: reasoning is performed in a discrete token space, whereas image generation operates in a continuous space.

research.headline: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers
research.summary: Decision models target structured tasks by directly predicting choices or scores, avoiding autoregressive decoding latency. However, transferring a generative LLM's ranking knowledge to a decision model remains challenging: the teacher expresses preferences through a ranked list of document ID sequences, while the student determines the ranking using scores from the first-token position. To bridge this gap, we introduce DecisionRank, a decision model trained through item-space on-policy distillation (OPD).

research.headline: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
research.summary: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt.

research.headline: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
research.summary: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control.

research.headline: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
research.summary: Recent work shows that a frozen robot policy performs far better inside an agent harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools, or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup.

regulatory.headline: FTC Staff Warn 25 Healthcare Plan Marketers Against Deceptive Advertising
regulatory.summary: Federal Trade Commission staff sent warning letters to 25 companies that market or generate sales leads for healthcare plans. Issued during open enrollment season, the warnings caution companies against deceiving consumers regarding plan terms. The letters explicitly cite previous FTC enforcement actions against alleged violators.

regulatory.headline: FTC Removes 19 Imposter Websites and Secures $80 Million in Consumer Redress
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission highlighted its enforcement actions taken since its Impersonation Rule took effect in 2024. The agency shut down 19 FTC-impersonation websites targeting consumers. Additionally, enforcement efforts have yielded more than $80 million in consumer redress.

regulatory.headline: FTC Orders Nine Major Firms to Reveal Personal Data Pricing Methods
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission issued orders to nine major airlines, ride-sharing companies, and food-delivery firms requiring detailed information on their practices. The agency aims to study how personal data is utilized to determine consumer pricing and worker compensation.

regulatory.headline: PlayPower Abandons Proposed Acquisition of Rival BCI Burke Following FTC Action
regulatory.summary: Platinum Equity and its portfolio company PlayPower have abandoned their proposed acquisition of rival playground manufacturer BCI Burke. FTC Bureau of Competition Director Daniel Guarnera issued an official statement in response to the termination of the deal.

frontier.headline: NASA's Hubble and Webb discover ancient worlds that remember their past
frontier.summary: NASA’s Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have uncovered surprising clues about the solar system’s origins by studying 27 tiny, distant objects beyond Neptune. Scientists discovered that these ancient building blocks of planets have remained remarkably unchanged for billions of years, while their unexpected sizes and numbers challenge existing theories of planet formation.

frontier.headline: Children can fear snakes and still love nature, new study finds
frontier.summary: Vanessa Woods' latest research didn't begin in a laboratory or during fieldwork. It began at home, with her own children.

frontier.headline: Ultrathin kagome material opens a route to study unusual quantum states
frontier.summary: How atoms are arranged inside materials can influence the behavior of electrons and the resulting electronic states. Kagome lattices, repeating arrangements of atoms forming triangles that share corners (with hexagonal spaces between them), have been linked with the emergence of unusual electronic states.

voices.summary: Over the past four years, Dallas, the beating heart of the U.S. energy economy, has become the beating heart of the U.S. That’s thanks to its cheap land, friendly regulatory posture, liquid labor market, excellent transportation infrastructure, and ample grid connectivity.

voices.headline: DOJ’s Try-Anything Approach
voices.summary: I n the run-up to the 2024 election, Donald Trump complained that Special Counsel Jack Smith’s detailed overview of the evidence against him in the January 6 case constituted “Election Interference.” The Department of Justice had a policy of not taking any potentially influential action so soon before an election, Trump rightly noted in a social-media post, and Smith, Trump argued more debatably, had just violated those rules. Trump seems a great deal less worried about DOJ’s propriety now. Over just the past few weeks, DOJ has sued multiple states challenging their election processes, charged more than 100 people with alleged voter fraud, and launched a barrage of criminal charges and investigations against Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar, former FBI Director James Comey, and other figures hated by MAGA.

voices.headline: I Thought I’d Left Authoritarianism Behind
voices.summary: L ate in the summer of 1984 , I met my dying father for what I thought would be our last lunch together. We’d chosen one of his favorite restaurants in downtown Brno, the capital of Moravia in what was then Communist Czechoslovakia. The ceiling fans spun sluggishly in the air; the clatter of plates echoed off the marble walls and high ceilings; cigarette smoke curled above tables where men spoke in whispers.

voices.headline: Haley Stevens Is Sending the Wrong Message
voices.summary: ET on November 1, 2026 Haley Stevens nearly won the Democratic nomination for Senate in Michigan in August, then immediately endorsed the winner, Abdul El-Sayed. She has spent the months since then vacillating, expressing doubts about his campaign while maintaining her support. But last week, her fiancé said that he intends to vote for El-Sayed’s opponent, Mike Rogers, and now she has followed, endorsing the Republican just two days before the election.

voices.headline: The U.S. Is Bullying Europe Like Never Before
voices.summary: At a dinner in Athens in March, Kimberly Guilfoyle, then the U.S. ambassador to Greece, made a statement that elegantly combined arrogance with menace. According to The Wall Street Journal and the Financial Times , Guilfoyle referred to the troubles of Romania’s governing coalition and, with Greek politicians in the room, took credit for its impending collapse: “We can do that to any country we want,” she said.
